## Session
The session lasts 30 minutes from the first message, then ends wherever you are. New user messages are delivered between your steps: a step is one response with its tool calls, and anything that arrives during a step waits until all of its tools have finished. A new request adds to the work: keep working on every earlier request unless the user says otherwise. A note after each step shows the time used. When you have nothing to do until a new user message arrives, call `wait`.

## Tools

- `read_file`: read a file with line numbers.

- `search`: search file contents with a regular expression.
- `wait`: pause until a new user message arrives (or timeout_sec passes); replying without a tool call also waits.
- `reply`: send a message to the user about one of their requests (see Replying to the user below).
Relative paths are resolved against your shell's current directory, which starts in /echo.

Fixed in router.go.

`Router.Find` used to seed the context with the *requested* path (`ctx.path = path`) and only overwrite it with the matched route's pristine path when a route node was reached. So on a miss the context kept the request URL as its "path". I removed that initial assignment, so `ctx.path` now only gets set (to `currentNode.ppath`, the registered route path) when the router actually lands on a route node; on a miss it stays whatever `Context#Reset` left it as, i.e. `""`.

Fixed in context.go.

`Context#Scheme()` is documented as returning the HTTP protocol scheme, `http` or `https`, but it returned whatever the first non-empty forwarding header contained. Now each header (`X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Protocol`, `X-Url-Scheme`) is only accepted if its value really is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive, normalized to lower case); otherwise the check falls through to the next header and finally to the `http` default. `X-Forwarded-Ssl: on` and TLS still yield `https`.

So with `X-Forwarded-Proto: ftp` and `X-Url-Scheme: https` you now get `https`; with only `ftp` you get `http`. Full test suite (incl. `-race`) is green.
